# Phase Three — Tiferes: Exact Execution Plan

The Awtsmoos renews every page and every packet before a selector or handler can claim a separate throne;
Awtsmoos.com will become futuristic by discipline first—each local root sovereign, each interaction complete, each API pathway known.

## Auth reference implementation
### Files to rewrite completely
- `style/auth/tokens.css` — move all auth variables from `:root` to `.login-page`; add semantic success/warning/danger/focus/state tokens.
- `style/auth/base.css` — replace raw `*`, `html`, `body`, `body::before`, `#BH` ownership with `.login-page`-rooted equivalents only.
- `style/auth/card.css` — root every shell/card/heading selector; keep atmosphere clipped inside auth page.
- `style/auth/fields.css` — remove raw `form`; root fields; add autofill, readonly, disabled, invalid, placeholder and focus-within state contracts.
- `style/auth/actions.css` — root every action; capability-gate hover; preserve active/focus-visible; add disabled/busy cursor/state semantics.
- `style/auth/status.css` — root status/busy selectors; add semantic status data-state affordances without requiring JS changes.
- `style/auth/responsive.css` — root responsive and reduced-motion selectors; add forced-colors fallback if kept here or split to accessibility.
- `style/auth/authUxContract.test.mjs` — reject known global selectors, verify root scoping, hover media gate, state coverage, import coverage, and file budgets.

### Files to retain unless evidence requires change
- `style/forms.css` — existing high-level manifest is valid if nested control imports stay explicit; rewrite only to improve covenant/ordering if status stays clean.
- `style/auth/controls.css` — nested manifest already separates fields/actions/status; preserve unless import contract changes.
- `login/index.html` / `register/index.html` — already expose the stable `.login-page` root; do not rewrite server logic during CSS wave.

## Shared future-system follow-up
- Re-run existing future-system contract.
- Audit all selectors for root sovereignty.
- Add a page-root adoption contract rather than global injection.
- Build an interaction-state detector test shared across future-system adopters.
- Extend controller JSDocs only by splitting modules when needed; never shrink documentation to satisfy 120 lines.

## JS/API follow-up
- Inventory page-level `fetch(` / XHR / request wrappers.
- Cluster by repeated behavior: JSON parsing, auth failure, loading state, abort, retries, status mapping.
- Extract one small request-result vocabulary only where actual duplication is proven.
- Keep renderer DOM code separate from transport and state.
- Require each touched function to document `@description`, every `@param`, `@returns`, thrown/rejected/error semantics, side effects, and lifecycle ownership.

## Verification order
1. Fresh exact-path git status immediately before auth writes.
2. Whole-file auth CSS rewrites only.
3. Readback all auth CSS files.
4. Run auth contract test and source line-budget checks.
5. Browser login/register at narrow + desktop widths.
6. Keyboard/focus/autofill/invalid/disabled simulation where browser tooling permits.
7. Only then generalize the sovereignty contract to the next page families.

## NEXT_ACTION
Run the fresh auth-path ownership check, then execute the complete auth CSS rewrite wave before tests.
